data.body: Ticket 4 (patriotic-abdicative-arrowana) plan-review PASSED after two rounds of correction: (1) render_findings_block already shows no severity per-finding (batch header conveys blocking/advisory structurally) so finding_publish.py needs zero change -- corrected my premise that it "prints an uppercased severity word"; wrong test-file references fixed too. (2) _render_review_text is SHARED between code-review (review_result, has decision) and scan-spec (spec_scan.py findings, severity-only, no decision) -- fixed to derive BLOCKING/ADVISORY from decision when present, fall back to severity when absent, preserving scan-spec's only signal. Real defect fixed in scope: adapter.py::_translate_findings flattens blocking+advisory with no distinguishing field -- now gets blocking:bool. Also obsoleted ticket broken-spirited-dorado (spec_scan priority migration) since ticket 6's scope was corrected to NOT remove findings.py's shared severity vocabulary (it serves an unrelated completion-verification module cluster with no priority alternative) -- spec_scan's _severity_rank/severity usage is therefore never broken by this epic. Rewrote tickets 5 (additive priority_threshold alongside fail_on_severity, since steps.gate isn't wired into any real production gate) and 6 (narrower: only stop review-kernel from stamping severity; relax review_result schema requirement to optional, not delete; findings.py/completion_verdict schema untouched) accordingly, and corrected the epic's own AC-3 to scope "every finding" to review-kernel findings specifically. Claiming ticket 4 now.
